rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4, 6.1-6.6, Tables 5-7 - the author builds an Arduino/GSM sensor prototype (soil hygrometer, DHT22, light, pH sensors), trains a KNN model on a constructed dataset and reports its own precision/recall/F1 and error-rate-versus-k results.
rows.notes: The study contains no EC or salinity sensor (sensors are soil moisture, air humidity/temperature, light and pH) and never measures salinity, soil condition or any salinity-related outcome. Its only results are KNN classification metrics (Tables 5-7) and a comparison of accuracy/RMSE with other published models. Nothing is reported on preventing over-irrigation or mitigating salinity. The pH-based fertiliser notification is a design feature, not an evaluated effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4, 6.1-6.6, Tables 5-7 - own prototype deployment and KNN model runs with reported classification performance.
rows.notes: No crop yield, growth or productivity data are reported; 'increased crop yield productivity' is asserted in Section 6.6 as a benefit without any measurement. No EC/salinity monitoring exists in the system. The study only reports ML classification accuracy (98.6%, RMSE 0.1) for the irrigation-need decision.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4, 6.1-6.6, Tables 5-7 - own prototype and KNN model runs with reported precision/recall/F1 and mean error versus k.
rows.notes: The abstract and conclusion assert that the sensors and weather forecast data 'reduce the amount of water used', but no water-use measurement, irrigation volume, or comparison against a control is reported anywhere. The reported results are only KNN classification metrics and error rates versus k compared with ref. [15] and [21]. The system also does not monitor EC. Thus no own evidence on preventing over-irrigation or water saving; the water-saving claim is an unsupported assertion.

notes: The paper is a prototype/ML classification study: it describes an IoT architecture, sensors (no EC sensor), a constructed training dataset (Tables 1-3) and KNN accuracy results. Field deployment is mentioned in one sentence with no field data. The 'results' are classification precision/recall/F1 and error-vs-k comparisons, not agronomic or water-use outcomes. Section numbering and table labels are inconsistent (two 'Table 6'), and some figures/tables appear partially garbled in the text.
